chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from some of our companions, he elevated the hadith, saying:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), when he intended to marry a woman, would send someone to look at her and say to the one sent: 'Smell her breath; if her breath is sweet, her scent is sweet. And look at her heel; if her heel is smooth, her calf is large.'

key_terms.كَعْثَبُهَا: Her calf (the fleshy part of the leg above the ankle)
key_terms.لَيْتُهَا: Her breath (specifically the scent from the mouth)

ai.seo_question: What physical signs did the Prophet Muhammad look for when choosing a wife?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith details the Prophet’s method for evaluating potential brides, where an envoy would assess physical attributes to infer general health and character. The specific focus on the heel's smoothness (*kathab*) and breath's scent serves as a practical indicator of bodily purity and vitality, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on both physical compatibility and inner goodness in marital selection.
